intro: Everything that could not be confirmed from an official source, plus every inconsistency found while reading one. Nothing here blocks the site; each item says what to do next. 'Unverified' is a state, not an estimate.

items.title: No 8 AM start exists in the official Venetian series
items.detail: The brief asks for a day that starts at 8 AM. Across all 94 published rows of DeepStack Extravaganza IV the earliest start is 09:10 (a satellite on Dec 12) and the earliest cash-prize start is 10:10 AM. The only 9 AM start found in any official Strip source is the recurring Horseshoe schedule; nothing published supports an 8 AM first event.
items.action: Either move the day's start to 10:10 AM (Venetian) / 9:00 AM (Horseshoe) or add a morning cash session; do not plan a tournament that is not published.

items.title: No Venetian structure sheet states a one-entry cap
items.detail: Ten sheets were read in full (1, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 11, 15, 18, 29). None of the one-day sheets contains a single-entry or 'no re-entry' clause; they state only a late-registration window. The Valuetown sheet (events 18/58) is the counter-example: it prices 'subsequent buy in's' at $200, which shows the room does write additional-buy-in rules when they exist. Silence is therefore meaningful evidence but not confirmation.
items.action: Get the answer in writing from the room (702.414.7657 / lv_cas_poker@venetianlasvegas.com) for the events you enter; the site keeps these rows as 'single-entry candidate', not 'confirmed'.

items.title: 23 of 37 structure sheets have now been read; 14 remain
items.detail: 13 more official sheets were read in full on 2026-11-17 (documents 2, 3, 4, 9, 12, 13, 14, 16, 17, 19, 20, 21, 22), on top of the 10 read on 2026-11-16 (1, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 11, 15, 18, 29). Every newly read sheet was cross-checked against its schedule-page row: buy-in, guarantee, start time, late-registration close and the Day 2 restart time agree on all 13 - zero mismatches. None of the 13 prints a rebuy, add-on or re-entry clause; sheet 4 prices a $20 house-fee discount for registering before the start of Day 1A, and sheets 2, 3, 4, 9, 12, 13, 14, 20, 21 state the multi-flight/Day-2-bagging rule instead. 14 sheets (23-28, 30-38 by document number: 23, 24, 25, 26, 27, 28, 30, 31, 32, 33, 34, 35, 36, 37) are still unread: their rows keep blank fee/stack/level/registration cells and the UNVERIFIED label.
items.action: Read the remaining 14 PDFs and add them to SHEETS in scripts/build-events.py, then re-run python3 scripts/build-events.py && python3 scripts/build-schedule.py && python3 scripts/build-site.py. The 2026-11-17 pass stopped because the document fetcher began returning signature errors for the remaining URLs; retry from a browser or re-run the job.
items.status: partly resolved - 23 of 37 read as of 2026-11-17

items.title: Wynn, Caesars, MGM, Bellagio and Golden Nugget rows are cited, not re-read
items.detail: Their values come from official documents read by earlier sessions on 2026-11-16 (recorded in research/e3cb221d-official-follow-up.md and data/verified/). This pass did not re-fetch them; Wynn's daily poster PDF is known to have returned HTTP 500 once. They are therefore excluded from ranking and shown only in the spend-advantage / unverified tables.
items.action: Re-read on the next refresh (the monitor will tell you if any of those URLs changed).

items.title: The Caesars guide is a recurring-format article, not a dated calendar
items.detail: It lists daily start times but no buy-ins, guarantees or entry limits for the Horseshoe schedule, and states the Caesars Palace $100 event has a $50 add-on for 15,000 chips at the first break.
items.action: Treat the whole Caesars block as 'verify the day you travel'.

items.title: No dated room quote is available for any property
items.detail: Every booking engine renders prices client-side, and this workspace blocks outbound requests to hotel hosts, so no rate could be captured for the actual stay dates. The Venetian also publishes poker rates only up to 150 days out.
items.action: Fix the dates, capture the itemised checkout total from the booking flow, and add it to the rate log; the calculator then stops being scenario-based.

items.title: Which number belongs to which hotel: '119 and 209'
items.detail: The official sentence is 'These rates will start as low as $119 and $209 and can be higher' for 'a Luxury King Suite in The Venetian or The Palazzo'. The order maps naturally to the order of naming but the page never says 'Venetian $119, Palazzo $209'.
items.action: Confirm with reservations (866.255.8936, code EPOKR25) before using either number as a budget.

items.title: Venetian states its resort fee two different ways
items.detail: Hotel Terms: '$55 plus applicable tax per night, payable upon check-in'. The 2026 poker suite-rate page: 'There is a $55 resort fee per night stayed' (no tax wording). The resort-fee page says 'Rates include a daily Resort Fee of $55 plus tax' per an earlier session.
items.action: The cost model taxes the fee (Park MGM's terms state lodging tax applies to 'any resort fee'), and the site labels that as an interpretation, not a quote.

items.title: Parking: two official statements, no reconciliation
items.detail: Hotel terms: registered guests pay $20/day. Poker room page: 'Complimentary Self-Parking - Enjoy convenient, free self-parking when you play with us. Non-registered hotel guests who play for three hours or more ... receive complimentary self-parking.' Whether a registered player's $20/day is also waived is not stated.
items.action: Ask the poker desk; the trip calculator keeps parking as an optional line so the estimate is not inflated or deflated by the ambiguity.

items.title: Venetian's 'Current Series' module is stale
items.detail: The poker page and the series overview still present 'WPT Fall Festival, October 28 - November 15, 2026' as the current series while DSE IV (which began Nov 16) is shown as the next one. The dated schedule page itself is correct.
items.action: Ignore the marketing module; use the dated schedule page. The monitor tracks this string so you see when it is fixed.

items.title: Bellagio Saturday sheet contradicts itself on the buy-in
items.detail: An earlier session recorded that the PDF heading says $1,100 while the file name says $1,000. Nothing is published here until the document is re-read.
items.action: Re-read and reconcile; until then the row shows blanks.

items.title: MGM Grand schedule PDF has no year and disagrees with the web page on the start time
items.detail: The PDF is titled 'August' with no year, and the Saturday event starts 11:10 AM in the PDF versus 11:00 AM on the page. Relevance to the Nov-Dec 2026 window is unproven.
items.action: Do not build a day around this event until a dated schedule is published.

items.title: Zero verified walking durations for every hotel-to-poker-room pair
items.detail: Official sources describe routes (Venetian/Palazzo indoor directions; the Bellagio-Cosmopolitan-Vdara interior bridge) but publish no minute values, and no map-provider access exists in this environment. The 30-minute rule therefore cannot be applied to any pair yet; the filter shows 'unknown' rather than a pass.
items.action: Run the pair through Google/Apple Maps once (links are on the walking page) and record the minutes in site-data/walk.json - or approve suggestion S-06 to automate it.

items.title: Quality floor cannot be set from official sources
items.detail: 'Cost and quality of hotel are higher priority than distance' needs a quality measure. No hotel publishes a star tier on its own reservation pages, and third-party ratings (Forbes, AAA) are outside the official-source rule this repo follows.
items.action: Choose a rating source (suggestion S-04). Until then quality cells are blank and the ranking uses cost + fee certainty + walk status only.

items.title: The 13.38% figure comes from a 2016 county notice
items.detail: The county document adopting 13.38% (12.0% + 0.5% LVCVA + 0.88% stadium) is dated November 15, 2016, effective for lodging nights from January 2017. The Venetian's own current terms still say 13.38%, so the rate is corroborated, but the county PDF is old.
items.action: Re-confirm with the Clark County Department of Business License before any non-refundable payment.

items.title: Earlier datasets attributed structure-sheet values to the schedule page
items.detail: data/tournaments.json carried reg_closes / chips / level on rows sourced only to the schedule page, and another session flagged them as not reproducible from that page. They are real values, but they come from the structure sheets (verified: '$90 of the $600 Buy-In... Late Registration: 10 levels + Break (~ 4:55 PM)', starting stack 40,000, 30-minute levels). The consolidated dataset attributes each value to its own document.
items.action: Use site-data/events.json; the old files are kept for audit only.

items.title: Earlier datasets called rows 'verified single-entry' on silence alone
items.detail: data/venetian-dse4-official-check.json lists 47 rows as single_entry and data/verified/tournaments.json lists 32, each justified by 'sheet read: no re-entry or add-on clause'. Under the 'never infer' rule that is a candidate state, not a confirmed one (see FG-02). Also, flighted events were counted as single-entry rows because each flight is a separate buy-in.
items.action: Superseded by the three-state classification in site-data/events.json.

items.title: Three dashboards existed at once; consolidated into one
items.detail: The root site, /docs/ (session acd81e67) and /verified/ (session a22d577b) each rendered their own tables from three different datasets, so the same event could appear with different labels on one site. This pass made the root site canonical and removed the two duplicate front-ends; all their data files remain in the repo.
items.action: If you preferred the old /docs/ view, it is in git history at the merge of PR #7 and can be restored.

items.title: Change monitoring starts with no baseline hashes
items.detail: The refresh job runs on GitHub's runners, which can reach the hotel sites; this sandbox cannot (outbound access is limited to GitHub, npm and PyPI), so snapshot hashes are written by the first scheduled run instead of being pre-seeded here. The extraction side is not left untested: `node scripts/check_sources.mjs --selftest` runs all 34 tracked patterns from site-data/sources.json against text containing the sentences they must match, and both plan-verify.yml and plan-refresh.yml run it before doing anything else, so a broken pattern fails loudly instead of reporting 'no change' forever.
items.action: After the first run (06:30 UTC daily) the report page will show ok/changed/error per source.

items.title: Wynn's $55 fee text is written for specific room types
items.detail: 'This Resort Fee is only applicable to reservations for the following room types: Wynn Resort King and Wynn Resort Two Queens.' Other room types are not covered by the sentence read.
items.action: Check the fee line on your own reservation summary before comparing Wynn against Park MGM.

items.title: Buy-in convention for unread sheets
items.detail: For the 34 rows whose sheet was read, the buy-in is fee-inclusive ('$90 of the $600 Buy-In is withheld for house fees'). For rows whose sheet was not read, whether the published number is fee-inclusive or fee-additive is unverified, so their cost-to-enter is shown as the published buy-in with a caveat. Confirmed on the 2026-11-17 pass: for all 13 sheets read that day, the buy-in stated in the schedule-page event name equals the buy-in in the sheet's house-fee line, so no row needed to change.
items.action: Reading the remaining sheets closes this.
items.status: checked - no mismatch on the 13 sheets read 2026-11-17

items.title: Session branch naming does not follow the protocol
items.detail: The protocol asks for branches named session-<id>/<task>; Arena fixes each session's branch (this one is arena/72ca3e9d-poker2). Recorded again because every prior session hit the same rule.
items.action: None; naming deviation is environmental.

items.title: Sheet 13 cross-references a flight set that its own header does not cover
items.detail: https://www.venetianlasvegas.com/content/dam/vlvweb/casino/poker/deepstack/2026/structures/dse_nov_2026-structure_13.pdf is headed "Day B+D @ 5:10 PM" and its footer says "SEE OTHER STRUCTURE SHEET FOR DAYS A+C+F", while dse_nov_2026-structure_12.pdf (header "Day A+C+E @ 11:10 AM") says "SEE OTHER STRUCTURE SHEET FOR DAYS B+D+F". The six flights published for Event #26 are 1A/1C/1E (11:10, sheet 12), 1B/1D (5:10 PM, sheet 13) and 1F Turbo (5:10 PM, sheet 14), so at least one footer is stale. The dataset follows the schedule page, not the footers.
items.action: Ask the Venetian poker room which footer is correct before relying on the cross-reference; no published value in the dataset depends on it.

items.title: 14 sheets stay unread because the document fetcher failed mid-pass on 2026-11-17
items.detail: The 2026-11-17 re-read pass completed 13 of the 27 outstanding PDFs and then the fetch tool began returning signature errors for every remaining URL from the same host, including retries after a pause. The 14 unread sheets are document numbers 23, 24, 25, 26, 27, 28, 30, 31, 32, 33, 34, 35, 36 and 37. They are NOT marked verified and their rows stay blank + labelled UNVERIFIED.
items.action: Re-run the pass (browser save of each PDF, then transcribe into scripts/build-events.py) - the sheet URLs are stable and the build aborts if a transcription disagrees with the schedule page.
